basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Adduxitque ea ad Adam, ut videret quid vocaret ea. Non est cogitandum carnaliter quod ita'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Adduxitque ea ad Adam, ut videret quid vocaret ea. Non est cogitandum carnaliter quod ita adduxerit Deus animantia terrae vel aves ad Adam, quomodo solet pastor gregem minare suum de loco ad locum: sed magis intelligendum, quia sicut divina potentia cum voluit, haec de aquis creavit; ita etiam eadem occulto nutu suae potentiae quando voluit ad hominem conspicienda perduxit, quomodo etiam ad arcam Noe cunctis generis volatilia vel quadrupedia non hominis manu congregata, sed divinitus acta venisse, eamque intrasse leguntur, nescientibus quidem ipsis ad quid venirent, sciente autem homine, qui ea venientia in arcam, Deo adducente ac jubente, suscipiebat.
